segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Good morning everyone, this is the ADFH OMS session on commercial configurations, session two of the BRD series.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: The plan for today is the rate matrix, customer tiers, and the wallet configuration. Then open points from session one if time allows.

segments.speaker: Nadia Haddad
segments.text: Thanks Saaqib. Before we start, from the Food Hub side we want to confirm the customer tiers first because Finance keeps asking. We have three tiers today: tenant, registered customer and walk in.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Understood. In the OMS the tier sits on the customer record and drives the rate matrix. So each service charge can have a different rate per tier. Is a fourth tier for government entities needed?

segments.speaker: Nadia Haddad
segments.text: Not now. Government entities are treated as registered customers with a discount code. Keep three tiers.

segments.speaker: Omar Rashed
segments.text: One thing on the rate matrix. Parking rates change by time of day. Morning and afternoon differ. Can the matrix hold time bands or is it one rate per service?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Today it is one rate per service per tier. Time bands would be a change to the matrix model. We can note it as a requirement and I will confirm the effort with the team.

segments.speaker: Omar Rashed
segments.text: Please do. Without time bands the parking revenue will not match what the board approved.

segments.speaker: Nadia Haddad
segments.text: On the wallet. Tenants top up a wallet and services draw from it. The deposit policy is one month of estimated charges. Finance wants the deposit to be shown separately from the usable balance.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: So two figures on the wallet: held deposit and available balance. Drawdown only from the available balance. If the balance goes below zero the service request is blocked, correct?

segments.speaker: Nadia Haddad
segments.text: Blocked for new requests, yes. Requests already in progress continue.

segments.speaker: Karim Yousef
segments.text: From IT, the wallet balance must also be visible in the customer portal, and the top up goes through Maqta Pay like the other payments. We agreed that in the payments session.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Yes, same flow. Top up creates a receipt and the wallet ledger entry. I will add the ledger view to the BRD. Karim, can you share the portal wireframe for the wallet page by Thursday?

segments.speaker: Karim Yousef
segments.text: Thursday is fine.

segments.speaker: Nadia Haddad
segments.text: One concern. The charge code list from Finance still has around eighty codes without a service mapping. Until that is done the rate matrix cannot be completed. I raised this last week as well.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Noted as a dependency. Who owns the mapping on your side?

segments.speaker: Nadia Haddad
segments.text: Finance, Yara's team. I will push them for a date.

segments.speaker: Omar Rashed
segments.text: Also, the Farmers Market stalls. Are they a service in the matrix or a lease? Last session it was left open and it changes how we bill them.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Still open. My understanding from the CRM team is that stalls are short leases, so they would stay in CRM and not in the OMS matrix. I will confirm in writing.

segments.speaker: Nadia Haddad
segments.text: Please confirm, because Commercial thinks they are OMS services.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: To close. Decisions today: three customer tiers, wallet shows deposit and available balance separately, new requests blocked below zero, top up through Maqta Pay. Open: time bands in the rate matrix, Farmers Market stalls, and the eighty unmapped charge codes.

segments.speaker: Nadia Haddad
segments.text: Agreed. Next session is Thursday at ten for compliance configurations. Please send the minutes today if possible.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Will do. Thanks all.
